items.title: Escalating fighting in Yemen deepens food security crisis
items.summary: Renewed conflict in Yemen has triggered a surge in hunger that could have consequences in the wider region and beyond, the World Food Programme (WFP) warned on Friday.

items.title: Iran says Hormuz to remain closed until US meets conditions
items.summary: Tehran says reopening Strait of Hormuz has been its main goal, while the US continues to focus on nuclear talks.

items.title: ‘I have not lost my dreams’: Refugee education funding cuts threaten millions
items.summary: A teenage girl who fled war-torn Sudan for neighbouring Egypt and hopes to pursue a technology degree is an example of why countries must ensure that young refugees can continue to learn.

items.title: Ukraine war ‘a human rights catastrophe’ that must end, says Türk
items.summary: The war in Ukraine is a human rights catastrophe that is “growing and intensifying by the week” and threatening an even greater disaster across the region, UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk said on Friday.

items.title: Gaza: WHO appeals for massive aid influx ahead of winter
items.summary: Repeated delays in bringing lifesaving medicines, prosthetics and more from Israel into Gaza risk having devastating consequences on Palestinians who urgently need them in the war-torn enclave, the UN World Health Organization (WHO) said on Friday.

items.title: Arresting the Dangerous Descent Back into War in Northern Ethiopia
items.summary: Long-simmering tensions have turned to large-scale fighting after armed opposition groups in Tigray, Amhara and Afar launched a multi-pronged offensive against Ethiopian government forces. It is not too late to avert a return to costly, bloody war.

items.title: The Houthis’ Advance to Bab al-Mandab: Has Yemen’s War Returned?
items.summary: In this online event, Crisis Group and external experts discussed how the front collapsed so quickly and whether Saudi Arabia, the Yemeni government and Yemen’s neighbours can keep this round of fighting from sliding into a wider war.

items.summary: German chancellor visits Kyiv amid air raid sirens, pledging strong support as Russian strikes disrupt the capital.

items.title: U.S. Statement on Increased Tensions Between Ethiopia and Eritrea
items.summary: Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesman U.S. Statement on Increased Tensions Between Ethiopia and Eritrea Press Statement October 3, 2026 Increasing cross-border tensions between Ethiopia and Eritrea have the potential to affect the entire region. The Horn of Africa cannot sustain another military conflict and humanitarian crisis. A conflict jeopardizes ongoing U.S. collaboration on shared interests with both countries. We strongly urge Ethiopia and Eritrea to respect the sovereignty and territorial integrity of their neighbors, exercise maximum restraint and return to dialogue

items.title: Daily Press Briefing by the Office of the Spokesperson for the Secretary-General
items.summary: In Ukraine, another wave of attacks killed 12 civilians and injured nearly 80, according to local authorities, the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs reports. Homes, energy infrastructure and a Kyiv bridge were damaged, with power disrupted in six regions. Humanitarian access is also worsening, with 86 access incidents recorded in July and August, up 26 per cent.

items.title: Why Canada is preparing for a (long shot) US invasion
items.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney has said the military is running scenarios in the unlikely case the US invades Canada.

items.title: Russia’s nuclear plants are ageing. Who will pay to dismantle them?
items.summary: Moscow faces a huge decommissioning bill at home even as it expands its nuclear industry abroad.

items.title: Hegseth Speaks to Cadets Ahead of Air Force, Navy Football Game
items.summary: Secretary of War Pete Hegseth traveled to the U.S. Air Force Academy near Colorado Springs, Colo., where he addressed roughly 3,500 members of the school's cadet wing ahead of the annual Air Force vs. Naval Academy collegiate football game.

items.title: ‘Wars Must Have Limits’, Third Committee Told, as Delegates Warn of Poverty, Climate Pressures, Threats to Human Rights
items.summary: Climate change, poverty, conflict and rapid technological change are placing mounting pressure on social development and human rights, the Third Committee heard today, amid concerns over the role of the United Nations human rights system and the devastating toll of war on civilians.
